title: Walking Home with You Anime Reveals Visual, April 2027 Premiere
content:
Walking Home with You anime revealed a new visual along with an April 2027 premiere date on Wednesday. No further details on the studio, staff, or cast were announced as of this writing.

Mai Matsuda writes and illustrates the manga which the anime is based on. Futabasha’s Manga Action magazine has been serializing the title since 2023. Omoi is releasing it in English, describing the series as follows:

A fresh coming-of-age romantic comedy about taking the long way home, from Mai Matsuda, creator of Hikaru in the Light! Shun was the star of his middle school’s soccer team, until an injury forced him to give up on his dream. Now in high school, he’s adrift, with no real interests or passions … until he meets his oddball upperclassman Naoki. She ropes him into joining her unofficial “Hyper-Epic Heading Home Club,” a club with only one member dedicated to turning every walk home into an adventure. As Shun follows Naoki through her flights of fancy in search of elaborate detours, secret treasures, and anything else that catches her attention, can the Heading Home Club bring color back to his drab everyday life?

A commemorative illustration from Matsuda was also unveiled:

title: These 3 Zombie Anime Series Are the Pinnacle of the Genre (And They Have a Combined 48 Episodes)
content:
The zombie genre has become one of the biggest in the entertainment medium, and the anime industry is no exception. In fact, anime has at least a couple dozen zombie series, offering a variety of choices that could continue to entertain as long as you are up for watching them. But finding great ones among the sea of series can be a task, and this list narrows it down to the three essential zombie anime.

The following three zombie anime have a total of 48 episodes combined, with one anime having two seasons with 24 episodes and the other two having 12 episodes each. One of these anime has a completely different take on the zombie genre, while one is a classic survival series, and the last one is arguably the best zombie series there could ever be, as it explores something very peculiar with the zombie trope.

3) Zombie Land Saga

Not just on this list, but perhaps Zombie Land Saga might just be the most unique zombie series to have ever been created in anime or any other entertainment industry. This is because the series combines the zombie genre with the idol genre. It follows a girl named Sakura Minamoto, who always had the ambition of becoming an idol. However, fate had something else planned for her, as she immediately dies after mentioning her dream when she is hit by a truck. Now, revived as a zombie years later, Sakura finally gets to pursue her dream.

It follows several other zombie girls like her who are pursuing the same dream and are brought together by a manager who aims to help the girls realize their dreams. The essential plot of this anime is undoubtedly the comedy due to its absurd premise, but it also tells a pretty good coming-of-age story. If singing and zombies are something you like, then with two seasons and a total of 24 episodes, Zombie Land Saga will provide you with a pretty fun ride.

2) Highschool of the Dead

Highschool of the Dead might just be the most accessible zombie anime for fans of the genre, even if they are unfamiliar with how anime depicts its narratives. It depicts the apocalyptic world that Western media often presents in such stories. Featuring a group of high school students determined to survive the outbreak, the series showcases their resolve during such a difficult time, immediately beginning with the protagonist making a tough decision.

With its added over-the-top elements, the anime also features some pretty amazing action sequences that many anime series come up with on their own. However, especially for fans who are not familiar with how some anime can use fanservice, it can sometimes be a little too much. That said, with only 12 episodes, it is the perfect zombie anime series for fans to get into both the zombie and anime genres.

1) Zom 100: Bucket List of the Dead

Zom 100: Bucket List of the Dead isn’t just the best zombie anime , but it is also one of the best modern anime series as well. With BUG FILMS at the helm, this anime features a protagonist who is actually happy about the sudden zombie pandemic, and all of this is because it finally helps him escape from the dark and draining job he has been stuck in for years. After realizing what the world has come to, Akira decides to make a list of 100 things to do before he is turned into a zombie.

Thus begins Akira’s journey across Japan in the apocalyptic world as he continues to scratch one entry after another off his list. There is only one season of the anime with just 12 episodes, and while it might seem easy to get into because of the small number, I’m pretty sure you will end up wanting more from the series, as the 12 episodes are only the beginning of a narrative that creates a fantasy of what you would do if you weren’t restrained and could do anything you wanted. Zom 100: Bucket List of the Dead is indeed the pinnacle of not just zombie anime, but zombie series in general, and everyone should watch it at least once.

title: You Are a Four Leaf Clover Romantic Suspense Manga Ends on October 15 (Updated)
content:
Retailers are listing the 12th compiled book volume of Koushi 's You Are a Four Leaf Clover ( Kimi wa Yotsuba no Clover ) manga as the final volume. The volume will ship on December 8. Update: This year's 45th issue of Akita Shoten 's Weekly Shōnen Champion revealed on Thursday that the manga will end in the magazine's next issue on October 15.

The romantic suspense manga centers around Uichi, a once popular student who is now relentlessly bullied in high school. Still, he strives everyday to keep a promise to Yotsuha (his first love from elementary school before she transferred schools) to become a veterinarian. Just as he reaches his limit with the bullying, Yotsuha suddenly appears before him. She has seemingly not changed since back then — except she harbors only one hidden resolve deep in her eyes.

Koushi launched the manga in Akita Shoten 's Weekly Shōnen Champion magazine in July 2024. Akita Shoten published the manga's 11th compiled book volume on Wednesday.

The manga is inspiring an upcoming anime .

Update: Added end date for manga. Source: Weekly Shōnen Champion issue 45

title: 'I Don't Want to Be Killed by You, My Crown Prince!' Manga Enters Final Arc
content:
Nao Oshiba revealed on X/Twitter on Tuesday that their I Don't Want to Be Killed by You, My Crown Prince! ( Ōtaishi-sama, Watashi Kondokoso Anata ni Korosareta Kunai ndesu! ) manga is entering its final arc and climax.

Not-so-wealthy noble young lady, Liesel, is set up by the foul-natured Blessed one and killed by her betrothed, the crown prince. Yet, when she awakens, she isn't in the afterlife. Instead, she's a child again with a second chance at life! This time around, she's changing her fate by becoming a powerful, talented magician in order to stay as far away as possible from the Crown Prince and the Blessed One. At least, that's how it was supposed to go... This time around, those who used to be enemies oddly approach her, and events that differ from how she recalls them keep occurring...

Oshiba's manga is an adaptation of Ema Okadachi 's original story. Oshiba launched the manga in Kodansha 's Palcy app in December 2021. Kodansha published the manga's ninth compiled book volume on February 27, and it will publish the 10th volume on October 29.

Okadachi began serializing the original story in the Shōsetsuka ni Naro website in February 2021, and ended it in March 2021. Kodansha published the story's print version in December 2021, with illustrations by Makoto Senzaki .

title: The Last Blossom Film Rescreens in Theaters on October 13 After Previous Screenings Had Incorrectly Timed Subtitles
content:
GKIDS had initially planned to only screen the film on August 30-31. However, theatergoers had posted that English subtitles were off by several seconds during screenings for the first day, and some screenings had been cancelled for the second day. ANN reached out to GKIDS at the time. GKIDS confirmed with ANN that it was reviewing its options and possible makeup screenings of the corrected verision.

The company issued a statement during that time responding to fans' complaints regarding the incorrectly timed subtitles and the consequent screening cancellations:

"On Sunday [August 30], GKIDS became aware of a subtitling glitch in our DCP for The Last Blossom . We immediately instructed theaters to remove shows from sale and issue refunds to affected customers until we could identify and resolve the issue. On Monday [August 31], we were able to provide a corrected version of the film to theaters. While some were able to update their screenings, others were unfortunately unable to do so in time, resulting in canceled shows. We deeply apologize for this issue and to all moviegoers affected, whether you attended a screening or had one canceled. We brought The Last Blossom to cinemas because it is a distinctive and wonderfully original work, and we are sorry that we fell short of the presentation that audiences expect. GKIDS believes the theatrical experience is central to film culture, and we know the time and sacrifice fans make to share this experience together. We are currently reviewing options including makeup screenings of the corrected version, to ensure audiences can experience this special film. Thank you for your patience and support as we work to put this right."

GKIDS describes the story:

Former yakuza Akutsu is serving life in prison after a middling career in the underworld. On the night he lays dying in his cell, he reminisces with his only companion, a smart-mouthed flower growing out of a can, about the choices that brought him here, the woman he loved, and a child he would give everything to protect. Is redemption out of reach?

Kaoru Kobayashi and Junki Tozuka both play protagonist Minoru Akutsu at both his past and present, respectively. Hikari Mitsushima and Yoshiko Miyazaki similarly voice Akutsu's partner Nana Nagata at different points in her life. Pierre Taki voices the talking Housenka flower.

Kinoshita directed the film, with Konomoto credited for the script and the original concept. CLAP ( Pompo: The Cinéphile , The Tunnel to Summer, the Exit of Goodbyes ) was in charge of animation production, and Michinoku-Toge drafted concept art. The band cero composed the film's music and performed the film's theme song "Moving Still Life."

The film opened in Japan in October 2025. The film played in the Feature Film Competition at last year's Annecy International Animation Film Festival in June 2025. A preview of the film was part of the Work in Progress lineup in last year's Annecy Film Festival.

Kinoshita and Konomoto previously collaborated on the ODDTAXI anime from 2021.

title: New Shonen Jump Series Is the Mob Psycho Replacement Fans Never Knew They Needed
content:
As the Fall 2026 anime season has arrived, the anime industry is seeing the release of new series, but Shonen Jump , as the leading manga magazine, is also bringing in new works. In particular, Shueisha’s Shonen Jump+ platform continues to provide new manga, once again proving the platform’s ability to feature interesting series. The latest manga debuting comes from the mangaka who has already created two comedy series, Sachi’s Records: Sachi’s Book of Revelation and Watch Out! Death Flag! . The creator, Chanta, has built a reputation for creating quirky series, and their return with the new series, Noro-Noro Puku-Puku , continues that reputation.

Chanta’s latest manga, Noro-Noro Puku-Puku , which launched as an English Simulpub on Manga Plus on October 5 in the West, comes with the unique style the author has presented in their previous works. The series features a cursed shrine maiden, Suzu, who is cursed by the gods themselves due to her behavior as a shrine maiden, taking advantage of people who fear the curses to make money. The judgment given to her perfectly sets the tone of the series, and it feels somewhat similar to an element that Mob Psycho 100 presented through its narrative and a character.

Comedy Manga Creator’s New Shonen Jump+ Series Is the Perfect Mob Psycho Replacement

One of the best elements of Mob Psycho 100 was its placement of comedy among the curses and Mob’s journey as a psychic exorcising them. In particular, the character who made the series feel more comedic was Arataka Reigen, who was clearly a con artist taking advantage of people afraid of curses. He was lucky to have Mob work for him, allowing him to maintain his status as a con artist for a long time. The premise of a con artist among curses and exorcism is what Shonen Jump+’s new series, Noro-Noro Puku-Puku , presents with its main character, taking it in a way that fans might have liked to see Reigen receive some divine and comedic punishment for being a con artist .

Suzu is immediately subjected to divine punishment from a god, where she has to exorcise 108 curses in total if she wants to keep living, with a cat named Puko attached to her head. The rest of the pilot chapter then sees Suzu following this punishment as she helps get rid of her classmate’s curse. The whole process is presented with perfect comedic timing, as Suzu showcases her desperation to get rid of her classmate’s curse, caring more about herself than actually helping her classmate. Suzu even tells her classmates to continue getting cursed so that she can complete her task immediately.

It is a perfect first chapter that presents a protagonist who is a con artist and now has to actually do the job as punishment, a premise that anyone will find amusing. Chanta has been known for presenting intriguing yet funny series, and this latest one is living up to that reputation. With elements that subtly reference Mob Psycho 100 as well, there couldn’t be a much better new series for anyone to start reading on Shonen Jump+.

title: Sony Pictures Entertainment Launches Crunchyroll Storyworks Division for Anime, Live-Action Adaptations
content:
Crunchyroll Storyworks is seeking to provide projects that can be greenlit for HAYATE Inc., the new anime production venture from Aniplex and Crunchyroll .

HAYATE Inc. was founded in March 2025 and is headquartered in Tokyo. Aniplex 's Masanori Miyake leads the venture as Chairman and CEO along with President and COO Leo Watanabe . The staff is composed of Aniplex and Crunchyroll employees. HAYATE is focusing specifically on planning, developing, and producing anime content for Crunchyroll 's streaming platform worldwide. In April, HAYATE acquired all shares of anime studio Lay-duce , making it a wholly owned subsidiary.

Crunchyroll increased the prices for all of its subscription tiers in the U.S. in February, and Crunchyroll halted free ad-supported streaming on its service last December.

Crunchyroll is an independently operated joint venture between U.S.-based Sony Pictures Entertainment and Japan's Aniplex . Sony Pictures Entertainment and Aniplex 's Sony Music Entertainment (Japan) parent are both in turn subsidiaries of Tokyo-based Sony Group .

Sony 's Funimation Global Group completed its acquisition of Crunchyroll from AT&T on August 9, 2021, after the company first announced the acquisition in December 2020. The purchase price was US$1.175 billion, and the proceeds were paid in cash at closing. Funimation 's home video releases are now listed under Crunchyroll .
author: ANN

title: 20 Years Ago, Fans Never Expected to See This Dark Sci-Fi Anime Hit
content:
Mecha has always been a huge genre within the anime community, with classic series like Mobile Suit Gundam and Evangelion becoming global phenomenons with staying power that’s nearly unmatched. Much of the reason for this is that mecha anime are able to tap into conversations regarding the cost of militaristic conflict, political disagreements, and the human condition through the lens of over-the-top combat with flashy giant robots. Among series tackling these themes, none do so quite as well as Code Geass: Lelouch of the Rebellion , an original animation project from Goro Taniguchi and Studio Sunrise that released in 2006.

Code Geass takes place in a dystopian world separated into three super-powered nations: the Holy Brittanian Empire, the Chinese Federation, and the Europa United. As the story begins, audiences are dropped into this strange, alternate take on the 2010s just as the Brittanian Empire seizes Japan using a strange new weapon called the Autonomous Armored Knight, or Knightmare Frame. The Empire strips Japan and its citizens of their rights, renaming the newly claimed nation to “Area 11” and referring to its citizens as the Elevens. While there are a few alternate timelines as Code Geass begins branching into a franchise, this is the original story that introduced the iconic antihero Lelouch.

Code Geass’s Characters Are Perfectly Imperfect

The original anime primarily follows a tight knit cast of characters who are in the throes of the ongoing geopolitical conflict sparked by the Empire’s takeover of Japan, centralized around Lelouch vi Britannia: an exiled prince of the Empire whose younger sister, Nunnally, was blinded after witnessing the murder of their mother, Marianne. Lelouch believes the tragedies endured by his mother and sister were inflicted upon them by his father, the Emperor Charles zi Britannia, and despite Lelouch and his sister Nunnally being used by the Imperial family as political pawns in Japan, makes a vow to dismantle the empire at any cost. This plot is set fully into motion when Lelouch begins attending Ashford Academy under the alias Lelouch Lamperouge, where he comes into contact with a mysterious young woman named C.C., who grants his a mysterious power called Geass, which gives Lelouch the power to dominate the mind of anyone he comes into contact with.

Code Geass is a complex narrative with a number of running plot threads surrounding its characters, and Lelouch’s descent into tyrannical madness at the behest of his newly acquired ability constantly puts the people he cares so deeply for when the series begins in danger. His quest for revenge against his father leads him to taking up a new alias, Zero, and commanding a resistance groups who dub themselves the Black Knights.

Despite his best efforts to become a hero capable of liberating Japan, he’s forced to navigate conflicts with his best friend, Suzaku, various half siblings and other members of the Imperial family who stand in his way, and even the Britannian Empire’s military force as a whole. Watching Lelouch try, fail, and succumb to his violent nature as he is consumed by his vow for revenge is truly haunting to watch, and has aided in Code Geass feeling like a unique viewer experience when compared to its contemporaries.

Studio Sunrise Treated Code Geass Like A Labor of Love

Being an original animation project and not something that was being adapted from a manga or novel, there were many different teams working together to make Code Geass what it is today — especially in the art department. The character designs for the series were done by none other than CLAMP, a group of four female manga creators consisting of Nanase Ohkawa, Mokona, Tsubaki Nekoi and Satsuki Igarashi, a group of award-winning creatives behind massive series like Chobits , Cardcaptor Sakura , and Magic Knight Rayearth .

While CLAMP’s works had been adapted to animation in the past, Code Geass was the group’s first time working on an original project designed for television. Takahiro Kimura, Studio Sunrise’s in-house character designer, spent multiple days studying CLAMP’s signature art style, notes, and concepts to nail down exactly how each character would look as they were coming to life. The love put into the series can be felt, with the anime becoming a massive hit, managing to find itself hitting with nearly every demographic of anime fan imaginable.

Whether it be anime fans looking for a character driven political drama, high-stakes, fast-paced action and plot beats, or even those who like to dive into shipping characters with one another — Code Geass truly had something for everyone . By mid-2008, a year after the original series came to an end, the anime had sold over 900,000 physical units in Japan, with the anime also becoming a hit overseas, and was subsequently named one of the most popular contemporary anime series that had been released in the United States that year.

The award-winning series has received a number of spin-offs, including audio drama, light novels, and official manga adaptation, and even video games exploring different timelines and potential events. The series is massive, even now, with the series set to return in 2027 with a brand-new anime series, and the love put into its production and story is a testament to its staying power.

The Empire strips Japan and its citizens of their rights, renaming the newly claimed nation to “Area 11” and referring to its citizens as the Elevens. title: GKIDS Releases 100 Meters Anime Film on Blu-ray Disc on December 1
content:
GKIDS announced on Wednesday that it will release the anime film of Uoto 's 100 Meters ( Hyakuemu ) manga on Blu-ray Disc on December 1.

The Collector's Edition includes five art cards and a mini-poster. The disc release includes an interview with director Kenji Iwaisawa , a rotoscoping workshop, and scene breakdowns. Pre-orders are open exclusively on GKIDS ' online store.

The movie premiered in Japan in September 2025. The film ranked #8 in its opening weekend, and earned 102,666,040 yen (about US$694,700) in its first three days.

GKIDS screened the film in October 2025 in Japanese with English subtitles and with an English dub . The film also screened in Los Angeles that October.

The film held its world premiere at Annecy in June 2025. The Japan Society screened the East Coast premiere in New York that October with director Kenji Iwaisawa in attendance. The film won the runner-up award for Best Animated Film at the Florida Film Critics Circle Awards in 2025.

Tori Matsuzaka plays the gifted runner Togashi, while Shōta Sometani plays Komiya, a hard worker whose obsession with the 100-meter dash began when he met Togashi.

Kenji Iwaisawa ( ON-GAKU: Our Sound ) directed the film at Rock 'n' Roll Mountain . Pony Canyon , TBS TV, and ASMIK Ace are credited with production. Yasuyuki Mutō ( Tokyo Revengers ) wrote the script. Keisuke Kojima was the character designer and chief animation director, and Keikankun Yamaguchi was the art director. Producers include Yūsuke Terada , Yūki Katayama , and Akane Taketsugu . Hiroaki Tsutsumi composed the music for the film.

The band Official HiGE DANdism performed the film's theme song "Rashisa."

A preview of the film screened at Annecy International Film Festival in June 2024 as part of the festival's Work in Progress lineup. The festival described the story:

Togashi is born to run. As a kid, he is naturally gifted and wins every 100-meter race without effort. But in sixth grade, he meets Komiya, a transfer student who is full of determination but lacks technique. In teaching him, Togashi gives Komiya a new purpose: to win no matter what. Years pass by, Togashi and Komiya meet again as rivals on the track and reveal their true selves.

Uoto ( Orb: On the Movements of the Earth ) launched the Hyakuemu manga in Kodansha 's Magazine Pocket app in November 2018 as Uoto 's first series, and Kodansha published the manga's fifth compiled book volume in October 2019.
